title: Hourly rollout staffing stripmap and retro scrapbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact, hour-by-hour staffing stripmap for a medium-sized rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> general) plus a lightweight release-notes draft and a short retrospective 'scrapbook' section where on-call notes and quick fixes are logged. Intended for use by the deployment conductor and the day-of shifts as a single-pane working artifact.

Context:
- Target rollout: model-routing fallback v2 + batching throttle adjustments
- Customer impact: low risk (no schema changes), but customer-facing latency could spike if batching misbehaves
- TL;DR goal: get to 50% within 3h with staged health gates, sample telemetry at 1m and 5m intervals

Preflight (T-48h to T-0):
- Run smoke build for canary image: RF-3122 (linked) -> owner: Marcus
- Verify telemetry ingestion pipeline (traces + p95 tokens): run 'telemetry-garden' dashboard check -> owner: Ava
- Canary capacity reservation: ensure autoscaler warmup triggers are set for the canary pool -> owner: Sofia
- Feature flag created and validated in staging: flag id release/routing/v2 -> owner: Jordan
- Communication: post preflight note in #release-orchestra slack and tag infra on-call

Day-of checklist (stripmap) - Hourly cadence
Hour 0 (T0) - kickoff:
- 10m: Kickoff huddle (conductor, on-call infra, lead SRE, product PM) -> confirm rollback plan and pager rotation
- 15m: Deploy canary to 1% traffic in region A only. Annotate release timeline in the tracker.
- 30m: Smoke tests: 100 synthetic requests across typical seq lengths (short/medium/long) -> pass criteria: no >2% error rate, p99 within baseline+50ms.
- Continuous: monitor ingest of 'prefix-cache-hit' metric and 'batch-size' histogram.

Hour 1 (T+1h):
- Evaluate canary metrics at 1m and 5m aggregates. If stable, roll to 10% to region A and 1% to region B.
- Start gradual batch-config warmup (batching multiplier 1.0 -> 1.2). Observe token-per-second delta.
- Notify CS for surface customers in region A about low-risk rollout (pre-announcement).

Hour 2 (T+2h):
- 10% observation window complete. Run targeted A/B quality checks on 200 prompts drawn from golden set. Alert if quality metric drops >1.5% (metric = semantic-similarity regression on eval harness).
- If any anomaly, initiate immediate rollback to canary image and open postmortem channel.

Hour 3 (T+3h):
- If A/B checks pass and infra signals green, move to 50% in both regions.
- Switch on additional autoscaler pools if throughput climbs; ensure headroom of 20% CPU/GPU.

Hour 4 (T+4h):
- Maintain 50% for minimum 1h. Collect the 'batch-success-rate' and 'cache-efficiency' snapshots at T+4h and T+4h+30m.
- Prepare a release-notes blurb for PM review.

Hour 5 (T+5h):
- If stable, go to general rollout (100%) with soft ramp of per-route concurrency limits for 15 minutes.
- Begin closeout and handoff to steady-state on-call.

Rollback triggers (quick checklist):
- Spike in 5m error-rate >3% absolute over baseline -> immediate rollback to previous model variant
- p99 latency increase >200ms for two consecutive 5m windows -> pause rollout and scale up GPU pools
- Quality regression >2% on golden prompt set -> rollback and lock flag
- Significant KV-cache miss storm (miss rate >30% for 10 minutes) -> preserve canary until fixes

Quick runbook for rollback (one-liners):
- Flip feature flag to previous variant (conductor) -> notify infra to drain new pods
- Scale up previous autoscaler target to avoid cold starts (SRE)
- Post message in #release-orchestra with incident tag and short reason

Release notes draft (short):
- Title: model-routing fallback v2: more resilient serving paths and smarter batching
- Summary: This release improves fallback routing logic to prioritize low-latency variants when GPU contention is detected and adds a batching multiplier tweak that should reduce unit token cost for short inputs. No customer-visible model behavior changes expected beyond slight latency improvements.
- Impact: Reduced p95 latency in 35% of short-session traffic; optional cost savings for bursty workloads.
- Rollout plan: Gradual canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% across regions (see stripmap).
- Rollback: Immediate flag flip to v1 if latency or quality regressions observed.

Post-release scrapbook (working retro notes) - to be filled in during and after rollout:
- 2026-03-03 T+0:15 - Observed transient 4xx spike on edge A; traced to rate-limit config mismatch in edge-proxy. Quick fix: bump edge throttle and restart canary pool. Owner: Ava.
- 2026-03-03 T+2:10 - Golden-set quality dip to 1.8% (under threshold but notable). Investigation: small prompt-encoding rounding quirk in staging->prod artifact. Action: hold 50% longer, track with metrics. Owner: Marcus.
- Retrospective prompts: did we have enough synthetic coverage for long-seq tails? Did autoscaler headroom behave as expected?

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we add a dedicated 'batching dry-run' that validates cost estimates before target rollouts? (Proposed: yes, owner Jordan)
- Need a lightweight, standardized 'scrapbook' template to capture incident micro-notes. Add to repo: /release-engineering/templates/scrapbook.md
- Validate that CS pre-announcements don't trigger support channel spam for low-risk rollouts.

Appendix: quick comm lines for day-of (copy/paste into slack)
- Kickoff: "T0 kickoff: rolling model-routing fallback v2 -> canary 1% in region A. Conductor: @Jordan, SRE: @Ava, Infra: @Marcus."
- Roll to 10%: "10% roll: canary healthy at 1% for 1h, moving to 10% region A + 1% region B. Watch p99 and cache-hit."
- Rollback: "Rolling back to v1 (flag flip). Reason: [short reason]. Pages: @oncall-sre @infra-team"

File notes: this is a working doc; please update the scrapbook entries in-place during the rollout. If anything becomes an action item, add a Linear ticket and paste the id into linked_artifacts.
